bizarre habits to make you the
most magnetic person in the room

the second hello

say hello twice: once when you arrive and once again later, by name. the second greeting feels personal, and people walk away feeling genuinely noticed by you.

the curious follow up

text someone the next day about something they mentioned: how did the interview go. tiny follow ups are so rare that people remember them, and you, for years.

the relaxed shoulders

before walking into any room, drop your shoulders and slow your breathing. tension is visible from across a room, and so is the calm that replaces it.

the odd fact

spend 5 minutes a day learning one odd fact: why the sky is blue, how octopuses think. a single strange fact is the easiest way into any group conversation.
slides.texte_sophia:
the odd fact

i used to stand at the edge of conversations. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, like how octopuses think. one odd fact gets me into any group.

slides.texte_overlay:
the slow exit

when you leave, stop, smile and say a proper goodbye to each person. rushed exits are forgettable, and a warm one is the last thing people remember about you.
